findings.description: The T-302 case 're-selecting the current program after a restore changes nothing' never selects a program before saving, so both instances are at program 0 and the case passes whether or not the #program line is written, parsed or applied. A wrapper whose setCurrentProgram applies a preset but never stores the index writes '#program 0' for every session.
findings.lens: technical correctness (state; tests pass while the product is wrong)
findings.conditions: a host re-applies the saved program after setStateInformation (the R-018 premise) and the index is not stored or is mis-parsed, which no test can see
findings.root_cause: the frozen test exercises only the default program
findings.traces_to: D-094; tests/juce/host_test.cpp T-302 program case; G-L1 question 4
findings.failure_path: S-310 and S-320 pass T-302 at program 0 on four runners; G-L1 question 4 reopens a session saved at the default program; after delivery a Live set saved with a non-default preset and edits reloads as the bare factory preset
findings.mitigation: Amend the T-302 case: setCurrentProgram(last), set every parameter to 0.37, save, restore into a fresh instance, require getCurrentProgram()==last, re-select it, require all values unchanged; add cases with '#program 99' and with no #program line; G-L1 question 4 saves with a non-default preset
findings.mitigation_adds: new frozen test cases (T-302 amendment through TEST_CHALLENGE route before implementation); one gate-question wording

findings.description: host-tsan uses tests/ci/tsan.supp when present; the file is not frozen and only prose restricts it. A TSan race: pattern suppresses a report if it matches any frame of either stack, so a pattern written for JUCE-internal reports (for example race:juce::) also hides wrapper races. There is no positive control that the build is instrumented, T-304 asserts only finiteness and counts, and a lock on the audio thread is invisible to TSan and every test.
findings.lens: technical correctness (real-time safety); integrity (bypassed test); CI coverage
findings.conditions: JUCE reports races at start-up under TSan and the implementer adds a broad suppression, which ENVIRONMENT section 5 permits with a deviation entry
findings.root_cause: the suppression mechanism is open-ended and the job has no canary
findings.traces_to: plan/ci/ci.yml host-tsan; plan/ENVIRONMENT.md section 5 (tsan.supp row); tests/juce/host_test.cpp T-304; D-094
findings.failure_path: S-003 and S-320: host-tsan green with a suppression that also matches wrapper frames; T-304 passes; autosave during playback races or blocks the audio thread in the shipped plugin
findings.mitigation: Freeze tests/ci/check_tsan_supp.py (each line 'race:' plus one fully qualified juce:: function, no wildcard, no Folk/folk symbol) run before the TSan step; freeze a canary program with a deliberate race that must exit non-zero under the job's TSAN_OPTIONS; S-REVIEW greps plugins/ for mutex, lock, CriticalSection and ScopedLock reachable from processBlock
findings.mitigation_adds: two new frozen files (checker, canary); one CI step; one review check

findings.description: The control pair is the reference against itself low-passed at 2 kHz, but the question asked is 'which side is the real instrument': both sides are real recordings, and a listener who believes synthesis sounds too bright picks the dull side. After two void attempts D-053 offers 'repeat' and 'proceed-without-pairs: <text>', which are not allowed responses of G-L1 to G-L5 in plan/GATES.md nor accepted by S-LISTEN's Done when; HANDOFF section 8 says only allowed responses count. Record names differ (S-LISTEN action 5: <gate>-round-<N>.md; D-053: -round-<N>-attempt-<k>.md).
findings.conditions: an attentive listener judges the low-passed side to be the real instrument in two attempts of one round
findings.root_cause: the control tests the listener's theory of synthesis, not attention, and the response lists were not updated together
findings.traces_to: D-053; plan/GATES.md G-L1 to G-L5; PLAN S-LISTEN actions 5 and Done when; HANDOFF section 8
findings.failure_path: S-LISTEN: two voids; the implementer must guess whether proceed-without-pairs counts (records it as a rescope) or stays halted; the gate is decided on remarks alone, which is the harm R-022 was meant to remove
findings.mitigation: Make each control unambiguously synthetic for the question asked (a sine driven by the reference's pitch and envelope, or the reference time-reversed); add 'repeat' and 'proceed-without-pairs: <text>' to GATES.md and S-LISTEN Done when, with the record stating the gate has no blind result; align record names. Done before any listening, so nothing is relaxed
findings.mitigation_adds: amendment of D-053, GATES.md, S-LISTEN; change in tools/build_evidence.py; no frozen test

findings.description: S-REVIEW and S-ADVERSARIAL precede S-LISTEN. Code changed afterwards by DR-12 iterate rounds (up to 3 per gate, 5 gates), by G-L1 question 4 wrapper fixes (state, MIDI, threading) and by the S-INTEGRATE merge of origin/main is never reviewed by a fresh context; only the frozen suite is re-run, and the pull request links the earlier reviews as the review of the delivered code.
findings.conditions: any iterate response or any G-L1 question 4 defect report, both expected uses of the gates
findings.root_cause: review placed before the last code-changing phase with no delta review
findings.traces_to: PLAN S-REVIEW, S-ADVERSARIAL, S-LISTEN, S-INTEGRATE; DR-12; GATES G-L1 question 4
findings.failure_path: S-REVIEW passes on commit X; S-LISTEN iterates change the reed model and the wrapper; DR-12 re-runs only frozen tests; S-INTEGRATE Done when checks CI only; an allocation or lock added in a fix ships while the records say reviewed
findings.mitigation: New step S-REVIEW-DELTA before S-INTEGRATE: if git diff <reviewed commit>..HEAD over core, plugins, tools, presets and CMakeLists.txt is non-empty, a fresh-context reviewer reviews it under S-REVIEW's rules (Critical and High fixed or taken to G-004); the pull request names the reviewed commits
findings.mitigation_adds: one step; gate G-004 when needed; no frozen test

findings.description: On a TinySOL cache hit the download and md5 step is skipped in ci.yml and gate-evidence.yml; only the count (689 files) and the metadata md5 are checked. T-200 measures about 100 accordion files that nothing hashes; fetch_references.py re-checks only the 12 indexed rows.
findings.lens: dependency and supply-chain drift; integrity (silently wrong results)
findings.conditions: a cache entry for the key is created by a run whose step chain was compromised (any job on the branch may create the key on a miss) or is otherwise altered
findings.root_cause: the integrity check is attached to the download, not to the data that is used
findings.traces_to: plan/ci/ci.yml reference job (cache, download, 'Reference notes exist'); plan/ci/gate-evidence.yml; tests/py/test_reference.py T-200
findings.failure_path: Cache hit; download step skipped; 689 files counted; T-200 compares the candidate with altered notes and passes; S-330 and S-REVIEW see green
findings.mitigation: Commit references/tinysol-accordion.sha256 (689 lines from the verified archive) and run sha256sum -c on it after the cache step in both workflows, failing the job on any mismatch
findings.mitigation_adds: one data file; one CI step per workflow; no frozen test

findings.description: make_blind_pairs.py draws rng.sample(stems, 14) then one rng.random() per pair, so the A/B key depends only on the seed and pair count: seed 10 gives ABBAAAAABAAAAA for all five gates (seed 20 ABAABBAABBAAAA, seed 11 ABBBBAABBBBAAB; simulated). D-053 fixes the seeds publicly, S-LISTEN action 5 commits decoded results per gate, and gates may be open together, so one decoded key reveals the others and the control positions for instruments whose stems sort alike.
findings.conditions: two or more gates have pairs (accordion and mandolin) and the owner sees one gate's decoded record before answering another
findings.root_cause: the seed schedule ignores the gate; decoded keys are committed while other gates are open
findings.traces_to: D-053 seeds; PLAN S-LISTEN actions 1 and 5; tools/listening/make_blind_pairs.py; HANDOFF section 9
findings.failure_path: G-L3 round 1 scored and committed; G-L2 round 1 uses seed 10 and the same key; control positions known; a careless listener passes controls and the void rule
findings.mitigation: Derive each seed from a per-round secret outside the repository (commit its sha256), or at least make it depend on the gate; commit decoded keys only after all five gates are closed
findings.mitigation_adds: S-LISTEN and D-053 change; no frozen test

findings.description: C-049: the Philharmonia mandolin type is not stated, so S-REF leaves 'sets' empty and T-201 renders the default f-hole body; when T-201 fails, DR-07 calibrates the global eta_E and plectrum factors (shared with the bouzouki) and the f-hole body's Q and gains against what may be a bowl-back recording.

summary: Round 2 (fresh context). The simulation: sessions saved with a non-default preset reload as the bare preset, the accordion drops out on autosave, and the listening records claim a blind result they do not have, although every Done when passed. New: 8 open (Critical 1, High 1, Medium 5, Low 1) plus 1 speculative (Medium, not counted). Residual: 7 (Critical 1, High 2, Medium 3, Low 1). Restated: 12. Round 1's mitigations that work: locale-independent state text (T-016), safe extraction (T-211), the split gate-evidence workflow, hash-locked installs, the host-test count, the T-303 wrapper equivalence, DR-16 naming all-green. Mitigations that can pass while not working: the T-302 program case (it only ever tests program 0), host-tsan (an unfrozen suppression file and no positive control), the listening control pairs (ambiguous for the question asked, and their void route leads to responses the gates do not allow), and the seed schedule (one key for all gates). Also new: reviews do not cover code changed during listening, and a TinySOL cache hit skips every integrity check.
